-83.13920,42.54860.name: Brenda L. Moskovitz, MD, PC
-83.13920,42.54860.desc: A fertility clinic reporting to the CDC's National ART Surveillance System. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. Reporting is required of every US clinic performing assisted reproduction, under the Fertility Clinic Success Rate and Certification Act, so this is close to a complete register rather than a list of members. What it records is cycles started, which is not the same as children born.

8.97072,45.55365.name: Accelera Srl
8.97072,45.55365.desc: An organisation accredited by AAALAC International for its care and use of laboratory animals. Accreditation is voluntary and paid for, so this is a list of organisations that chose to be inspected rather than a register of everyone doing the work. An organisation absent from it is not accredited; that says nothing about whether it uses animals. In several countries the largest users are absent for exactly that reason. The directory gives a city and country and no street address, so this point marks where the organisation is registered rather than the building where animals are held.

-0.40442,50.80660.name: Agora Clinic Worthing
-0.40442,50.80660.state: Phoenix Medical Centre, Lime Tree Surgery Goring, 4 The Waterfront, Worthing, BN124FD
-0.40442,50.80660.company: Satellite clinic to Agora Clinic Brighton
-0.40442,50.80660.desc: A fertility clinic licensed and inspected by the Human Fertilisation and Embryology Authority. Satellite clinic to Agora Clinic Brighton. A satellite is where patients are seen; the licence sits with the parent clinic, so the regulator's paperwork and the treatment are in different places. A fertility clinic is where human embryos are made, selected and stored, and where assisted reproduction happens, like IVF, ICSI, egg and sperm donation, freezing embryos and eggs for later. The HFEA licenses every clinic in the United Kingdom, inspects them, and publishes findings and success rates clinic by clinic. No other fertility regulator publishes at this level, which makes the UK the one country where this sector can be read rather than estimated.

-123.95539,49.21057.name: Pacific Biological Station
-123.95539,49.21057.status: Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, September 2025
-123.95539,49.21057.desc: An institution certified by the Canadian Council on Animal Care for its use of animals in science. A site of Fisheries and Oceans Canada. Certificate of GAP Last visit: interim, September 2025. CCAC certification is a condition of federal research funding rather than a licence, so an institution outside it is not necessarily outside the work — it may simply not take federal money. The CCAC publishes names and certificate status and no addresses, so this point marks the institution rather than the building where animals are held.

-71.28100,42.46800.name: Thermo Fisher Scientific
-71.28100,42.46800.desc: The largest life-sciences supplier in the world by revenue, selling the instruments, reagents and cell-culture media that nearly every laboratory on this map depends on daily. Through Patheon it also manufactures drugs for other companies, and through PPD it runs their clinical trials, so the same firm can supply the materials, make the product and test it in people. Almost no engineered organism anywhere is made without something from this company, which makes it infrastructure rather than a participant — and infrastructure is rarely regulated as an actor. It is also the company that sold DNA collection kits used in Xinjiang, which it withdrew after sustained pressure.

-6.15000,53.29000.name: ICON plc — site and patient networks
-6.15000,53.29000.state: Dublin — South County Business Park, Leopardstown
-6.15000,53.29000.desc: An Irish contract research organisation running trials worldwide, and the owner of networks of clinical sites and patient recruitment operations. Owning the sites as well as running the trial concentrates the study, the participants and the data in one commercial relationship, which is efficient and removes the independent check a separate site once provided.

-91.79200,43.35200.name: Seed Savers Exchange
-91.79200,43.35200.desc: A US non-profit maintaining thousands of heirloom vegetable and grain varieties and distributing them between members. Varieties survive by being grown, not by being frozen: a seed bank preserves a sample, and a network like this preserves the plant in cultivation and the knowledge of how to grow it. It is the practical counterweight to a commercial seed market in which a variety that stops selling stops existing.

8.69000,49.44000.name: EW Group
8.69000,49.44000.desc: A private German holding company that owns Aviagen — the other of the two broiler genetics companies — alongside layer, turkey and aquaculture genetics businesses. It is one of the most consequential animal-breeding groups in the world and among the least visible, because being family-owned it publishes almost nothing.

6.13700,46.22700.name: UPOV — the office behind the convention
6.13700,46.22700.desc: Administers the plant variety convention that 80 members and 99 countries are bound by, and advises governments drafting national seed laws — which is the quieter and more consequential half of what it does. A country acceding to the 1991 act typically works from UPOV's own model provisions, so the text that criminalises seed exchange in one country is recognisably the text used in another.
